Hill alpha is the tail index of the top 5% of claims (alpha < 2 means infinite variance); gpd_xi is the generalised-Pareto shape above the 95th percentile (xi > 0.5 means infinite variance); exp_claims_above_max = expected number of claims at least as large as the observed maximum among the exceedances, under the fitted GPD (a value far below 1 means the maximum is implausibly large for the rest of the tail).

## 5. What the single largest bodily-injury claim does to the motor level

- Bodily-injury excess load at the 99.9th-percentile cap: 0.0832 with the largest claim, 0.0076 without it.
- Bodily injury is 36.1% of capped motor cost, so that claim raises the model's motor level by about 2.71% (excess-load channel only).
